sentences.text: The petitioner has filed this petition U/Sec.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident that occurred on 29-08-2018.

2. The petition averments in brief are as under:
On 29-08-2018 at about 3.45 p.m., the petitioner was riding a Hero Honda Bike bearing No.KA-05-HE-0597 from Jayanagara to his house, near Canara Bank (C.B.)
junction, 9th main, 27th cross road, 3rd block, Jayanagara, Bengaluru, at that time the rider of the Honda Dio Motorcycle bearing No.KA-05-KF-9680 rode the same at high speed, in a rash and negligent manner, came from petitioner's right side,
jumped the signal and dashed against the petitioner' motorcycle and caused the accident.
Due to the said impact the petitioner along with his two wheeler fell down and grievous injuries all over the body.

Immediately after the accident, the petitioner was shifted to Apollo Hospital,
Jayanagara, Bengaluru wherein petitioner took treatment as an inpatient and also underwent surgery.
The petitioner has spent an amount of Rs.3,00,000/- towards hospitalization charges, conveyance, medical treatment, attendant and other incidental charges etc.,
Prior to the accident, petitioner was aged about 65 years, hale and healthy and was working as Supervisor under S. Ningappa PWD Class -I Civil Contractor in Bengaluru and earning Rs.25,000/- p.m.
Due to the accidental injuries petitioner is not able to do his work as he was doing prior to the said accident and thereby lost his earning capacity.
The respondent No.1 is the insurer and respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle, are jointly severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.

Hence,
prays to award compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- with interest.
3. After service of summons, respondents have appeared through their counsels.
But the respondent No.2 -owner has failed to file written statement.
The respondent No.1- insurer has filed written statement by denying the cause and manner of accident.

Further it has admitted the issuance of policy to the Motorcycle bearing No.KA-05-KF-9680 which was in force as on the date of accident and the liability of this respondent if any is subject to the terms and conditions of the policy.
It has contended that, there is no compliance of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of MV Act.

Further this respondent submits that the rider of the offending motorcycle was not holding valid and effective driving licence, in this regard the jurisdictional police have filed charge sheet under Sec.3(1), 181, 5 & 180 of MV Act.
Further it has also denied the age, occupation, income and injuries sustained by the petitioner and also the treatment taken for the injuries.

This respondent submitted that the claim petition is not filed in time and barred by limitation the alleged accident was taken place on 29-08-2018 whereas the claim petition has been filed on 04-06-2024 i.e., after lapse of 70 months, as such there is an inordinate Ramachandra vs Icici Lomb Gen Ins Co Ltd on 10 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/139945407/
2 delay on the part of the claimant in filing the claim petition.

sentences.text: Accordingly, prays to dismiss the petition against it.

4. On the basis of the rival contention, the following issues are framed by this court:
1.

Whether the petitioner proves that, the petitioner sustained grievous injuries due to the actionable negligent riding of motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-05- KF-9680 by its rider, in RTA took place on 29.08.2018 at about 3.45 p.m. near Canara Bank (C.B.)
junction, 9th main, 27th cross road, 3rd block, Jayanagara, Bengaluru?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed for?
If so, what rate?

From whom?
3. What Order or Award?
5.
In order to prove the claim petition, the petitioner himself is examined as P.W.1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P.1 to 11.
Further the MRO of Apollo hospital is examined as PW.2 and Ex.P12 to P.15 were got marked.
On the other hand, the respondent No.1- insurance company has examined its official as RW1 and got marked one document at Ex.R.1.

6. Heard the arguments of both sides and perused the material evidence that are available on record.
7.
My findings on the above issues are as under.

As per final orders  for the following:-
 : R E A S O N S:
 ISSUE NO.1 :
8.
That by reiterating all the averments made in the petition, the petitioner filed affidavit in lieu of- examination in-chief.

In support of his case, he has produced true copies of FIR, complaint, spot mahazar along with sketch, IMV report, wound certificate and charge sheet, all these documents are marked under Ex.P.1 to P.7.
9.
On perusal of Ex.P1- FIR is registered on the basis of first information given by the petitioner by alleging the rash and negligent riding by the rider of the Motorcycle bearing No.KA-05-KF-9680.
After the registration of FIR as per Ex.P1, the Ex.P3 & 4 spot mahazar and rough sketch were conducted.

On perusal of Ex.P3 spot mahazar, the accident spot is in the junction wherein the petitioner was proceeding in the left side of the road and rider of the offending vehicle came from cross road dashed against the motorcycle of the petitioner.

In the complaint itself it is alleged that Ramachandra vs Icici Lomb Gen Ins Co Ltd on 10 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/139945407/
3 rider of the offending motorcycle jumped the signal and violated the traffic rules, thereafter caused the accident.

sentences.text: Thereby it is evident that the rider of the Motorcycle bearing No.KA-05-KF-9680 was negligent.

The Ex.P5 is the IMV report wherein the Hero honda motorcycle bearing No.KA-05-AE-597 has got damages in its front side number plate bend, handle bend, right rear side deeky box damage, right side rear view mirror broken, on the other hand, offending motorcycle bearing No.KA-05-KF- 9680 has got damages in its front side shield, front side head light, front wheel mud guard, bend, right side rear view mirror broken, middle portion.
The contents of Ex.
P3 to 5 supported the case of the petitioner to prove the alleged negligence of the rider of the Motorcycle bearing No.KA-05-KF-9680.
If the rider of Motorcycle bearing No.KA-05-KF-9680 has not jumped the signal and violated the traffic rules the said accident was not going to be caused.

10. Ex.P7 charge sheet is also came to be filed on against the rider of the Motorcycle bearing No.KA-05-KF- 9680, and the IO has opined that the negligence is on the part of rider of the Motorcycle bearing No.KA-05-KF- 9680.
No other grounds are made out by the respondents to show the contributory negligence from the petitioner.
11. The respondent No.2 has filed written statement by denying the negligence and their liability.
In this regard the respondent No.2 has also examined its official as RW1 who had deposed on the basis of the police documents and has no personal knowledge about the accident.
As discussed supra, the petitioner successfully established the actionable negligence by the rider of the Motorcycle bearing No.KA-05-KF-9680.

Thus, by considering all these points this court is of the opinion that the said accident is caused by the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the Motorcycle bearing No.KA-05-KF-9680.
12.
The alleged accident is of dated 29.08.2018 but the FIR was registered on 01.09.2018 i.e., after 3 days of accident.

In this regard petitioner summoned and produced Ex.P14 MLC register extract where it evidentiates that on 29.08.2018 itself the petitioner admitted to their hospital at 4.35 p.m.
with a history of RTA.
Thus as per Ex.P.2 the petitioner assigned reasons for delay in lodging the complaint.
Thereby the delay of 3 days in filing the complaint is explained by the petitioner.
13. The first respondent who is the owner of the offending vehicle does not chosen to deny the allegation of the rash and negligence riding.

The charge sheet is came to be filed on the the rider of the Motorcycle bearing No.KA-05-KF-9680 for the offences punishable under Sec. 279 & 338 of IPC and also U/Sec 119, r/w 177 & 3(1) r/w Sec. 181 & 5 r/w 180 of MV Act.

sentences.text: In a claim for compensation under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the claimant is to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and the standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by Hon'ble Supreme Court in the decision reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319 Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others.

sentences.text: Further the Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others (2009) 13 SCC 530, wherein it is held that, it was necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.

sentences.text: The claimants were merely to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied.

15. In support of these documentary evidence, if we perused the oral evidence of the petitioner on this point, even though the respondent no.1 made a suggestions to the petitioner by denying their liability and alleged negligence, nothing being elicited or produced to probabalise the said defence.
16. The contents of Ex.P3 spot mahazar, Ex.P4 spot sketch and Ex.P5 IMV report helped the petitioner to prove his case.

In this context by considering the contents of Ex.P1 to 7 this court tilts in favour of the petitioner as the petitioner has to prove the alleged negligence on the basis of the evidence and proof of the same on preponderance of probabilities.
17. As per well settled principle of law, the standard of proof in the claim petition like the present is preponderance of the probability.
There are no grounds to disbelieve the case of petitioner in the absence of rebuttal evidence.

All the materials available on record leading to show that, petitioner has sustained injuries in the accident took place on 29-08-2018 which is caused by the driver of the Motorcycle bearing No.KA-05-KF- 9680 which belonging to respondent No.1.
There is no reason to discard the evidence of petitioner.

In the claim petition like present one strict proof is not necessary,
but preponderance of probabilities is sufficient.
Accordingly, issue No.1 answered in the affirmative.

ISSUE NO.2:
18.
As already held herein above, the petitioner has proved that he has sustained injuries in RTA which is caused by rider of offending motorcycle.
Hence, the petitioner is entitle for compensation.
Now the quantum of compensation is to be ascertained on different heads.
19. The petitioner has produced wound certificate as per Ex.P6 which shows that the petitioner sustained grievous injuries.
Further, the petitioner has also produced discharge summary marked at Ex.P8, which shows that, petitioner has sustained Base of first metatarsal fracture right side with soft tissue injury left knee.
The petitioner has not examined the doctor who treated him at the time of accident.
Without the evidence of doctor, it is not possible to believe that, the petitioner has sustained disability due to grievous injuries.
20. According to the petitioner he was working as Supervisor and earning Rs.25,000/- p.m.
But to prove his avocation and income, the petitioner has not produced any documents.

sentences.text:
While determining the compensation this court has to look into the pain and sufferings, medical expenses, diet, food, nourishment, attendant and conveyance charges and loss of amenities and enjoyment of life that the PW-1 has suffered, which are discussed herein below:
(A) TOWARDS PAIN AND SUFFERINGS:
The petitioner has relied upon Ex.P.6 - wound certificate and Ex.P8 discharge summary, which make it crystal clear that PW-1 has sustained grievous injuries.
The petitioner was admitted to Apollo Hospital on 29-08- 2018 and discharged on 01-08-2018.

Hence keeping in mind the injuries mentioned in wound certificate, it can be said that the petitioner must have undergone some amount of physical pain and sufferings, for which, an amount of Rs. 40,000/- can be held to be just and proper compensation under this head.
(B) TOWARDS MEDICAL EXPENSES:
The petitioner has produced medical bills which is marked as Ex.P-9.
In the cross-examination petitioner admitted that he is retired employee of NIMHANS hospital and the medical bills are got reimbursed from NIMHANS health care.
Further he has stated that Rs..10,000/- was spent by him towards some expenses.
But as per Ex.P.9 inpatient medical bill the entire medical bill is paid by NIMHANS health care scheme.
No bill are produced to claim the compensation under this head.
Hence, petitioner is not entitled for any compensation under this head.

(C) TOWARDS DIET, FOOD, NOURISHMENT, ATTENDANT AND CONVEYANCE CHARGES:
As already observed the Ex.P-8, makes it amply clear that the petitioner underwent treatment for the injuries sustained by him.
During the said period the petitioner might have taken assistance from others and taken diet food.
On consideration of the injuries sustained by the petitioner this Tribunal is of the opinion that it is just and proper to award an amount of Rs.15,000/- under this head.

(D) TOWARDS LOSS OF FUTURE EARNING CAPACITY ON ACCOUNT OF PERMANENT DISABILITY:
It is necessary to note that the loss of future earning capacity cannot be presumed and has to be proved with cogent evidence.

But interestingly the petitioner though claims that he is unable to do any work and has become permanently disabled he has not put in any efforts to prove the disability by examining the doctor, who treated him.
In fact he has not even produced the disability certificate issued by competent authority.
In the absence of any such material piece of evidence, it is very difficult for this Court to assess the disability and thereby assess the loss of earning capacity due to disability.
In the cross-examination the PW1 admitted that as he is retired employee of NIMHANS, he is getting pension and he is still receiving the pension through his bank account.

Hence, this court has no option but to hold that the Ramachandra vs Icici Lomb Gen Ins Co Ltd on 10 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/139945407/
6 petitioner has not suffered any permanent physical disability which has resulted in reduction of his salary/pension and hence he is not entitled for any compensation under this head.

sentences.text: (E) TOWARDS LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID UP PERIOD:

The petitioner has not made out any evidence or grounds to hold that he sustained the loss of income during the laid down period hence, in the absence of any evidence,
petitioner is not entitled for any amount under the head of loss of income during laid up period.
(F) TOWARDS LOSS OF AMENITIES AND ENJOYMENT OF LIFE:
The petitioner admitted to the hospital for the injuries sustained by him, which might certainly have deprived him of the basic comforts and enjoyment.
Therefore, it is just and proper to award him a reasonable sum of Rs.25,000/- under this head.

food, nourishment, Rs. 15,000-00 attendant and conveyance charges D) Towards loss of future earning NIL capacity E) Loss of income during laid up NIL period F) Towards loss of amenities Rs.
25,000-00 Total Rs.80,000-00 23. Liability:-

The respondent No. 1 in its objection statement has admitted the issuance of policy to the offending motor cycle bearing No. KA.05-KF-9680 and taken contention that the rider of the offending motor cycle was not having valid licence at the time of accident.
In this regard the official of respondent NO.1 insurance company is examined as RW.1 and produced the Ex.R1 .
The Ex.R1 is the copy of policy wherein it shows that the vehicle bearing No. KA.05-KF-9680 was insured with them from 09-12-2017 to 08-12-2018.
The date of accident is 29-08-2018.
As such as on the date of accident the offending vehicle bearing No. KA.05-KF- 9680 was duly insured with respondent No.1 - insurance company.
24. The respondent No.2 is the RC owner of the vehicle bearing No. KA.05-KF-9680.
The respondent No.2 appeared but not filed written statement.

25. Now that this court has ascertained the compensation amount, the last aspect of the matter is regarding fixation of liability i.e., who should be made liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner?

Precisely, it is the specific case of the respondent No.1 insurance company that owner has handed over the offending vehicle bearing No. KA.05-KF-9680 to a person who has not having valid driving license.

To establish the said fact, the respondent No.1 initially relied on Ex.P7 charge sheet wherein Sec.279, 338 of IPC and Sec.119 r/w 177 & 3(1) r/w 181 & 5 r/w 180 of IMV Act are invoked against the rider of vehicle bearing No. KA.05- KF-9680.
On perusal of the Ex.P7 the rider of the said offending vehicle bearing No. KA.05-KF-9680 was not having valid licence at the time of accident to drive the said vehicle.

sentences.text: The respondent No.2 owner even though appeared not lead any evidence by denying the contents of charge sheet in this regard.
Thereby the respondent No.1 insurance company discharged its burden to hold that the rider of the vehicle bearing No. KA.05-KF-9680 was not having valid licence at the time of accident.
27. There is no dispute that at the time of accident the vehicle was covered with insurance.
But the violation of the condition of insurance policy is stands established.

As per Ex.R1 it contains the condition that it covers the risk provided the person driving the vehicle holds an effective and valid driving licence at the time of accident and is not disqualified from holding such licence.

In this case,
the respondent No.2 owner of the offending vehicle bearing No. KA.05-KF-9680 not contested the petition by adducing any evidence by showing that the rider was having driving license at the time of accident.
28. The next aspect to be pondered upon now is, what is the effect if the rider of the offending vehicle not possessing a driving license at the time of accident.

29. In H.K. Shivaramu Vs. H.S.Shivaramum other rendered by the Division Bench of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka on 4.12.2020 wherein in a similar set of facts the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka held thus:

sentences.text:
10. On the basis of the evidence of the parties and the materials available on record,
i.e., Ex.P2 - charge sheet the Tribunal has rightly held that the rider of the offending vehicle was not holding a valid and effective driving licence and fastened the liability on the respondent Nos. 1 and 2 - the rider and the owner of the offending vehicle jointly and severally.

In view of the law laid down by a Full Bench of this Court in the case of YELLAVVA (supra), even though there is violation of policy conditions, when it is not in dispute that as on the date of the accident the offending vehicle was covered by the insurance policy, the insurance company has to pay the compensation with liberty to recover the same.

The essence of the said decision is that even where the driver of the offending vehicle was found to be driving without a valid driving license and the insurance company pleads that there is violation of policy conditions, if the vehicle had a valid and subsisting insurance policy, then the insurance company has to pay the compensation with liberty to recover the same from owner and rider.

30. In fact the Hon'ble Division Bench of the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka relied upon the decision of Hon'ble full bench of the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in New India Assurance Co.,
Ltd., vs Yallavva reported in ILR 2020 Kar 2239 equivalent (2020) 2 KCCR 1405 wherein the Hon'ble High court has reaffirmed the principles relating to pay and recover by relying upon decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Swaran Singh and Others reported in (2004) 3 SCC 297 cited supra held thus:

sentences.text: On a reading of the same, it becomes clear that the Hon'ble Supreme Court has laid down two tests.

The breach of a policy condition, for example, by disqualification of the driver to hold a driving licence or invalid driving licence has to be proved to have been committed by the insured for avoiding liability by the insurer.

In other words, in order to avoid the liability towards the insured, the insurer has to prove that the insured was guilty of negligence and failed to exercise reasonable care in the matter of fulfilling the condition of policy regarding use of the vehicle by a duly licensed driver or one who was not disqualified to drive at the relevant time.

Thus,
burden of proof of establishing breach on the part of the owner of the vehicle is on the Insurance Company.
The above is the first test laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court.
Then, there is another test enunciated.

Even after proving breach of a policy condition regarding a valid licence by the driver or his qualification to drive during the relevant period on the part of the insured, the insurer would not be allowed to avoid his liability towards the insured unless the said breach or breaches is/are so "fundamental" as found to have contributed to the cause of the accident.
This is having regard to the "rule of main purpose" or "main purpose rule" i.e., even if there is a proof of the driver of a motor vehicle not being duly licenced at the time of the accident,
the said fact must be a cause for the accident.
In other words, the breach was so fundamental as to have contributed to the cause of the accident.
The doctrine of fundamental breach has been incorporated in Section 149 of the Act by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in order to give effect to the main purpose rule.
Thus, the exclusion clause or the defence of an insurer so as to avoid liability has been read down to the extent to which it is inconsistent to the main purpose of the contract.
The above is the second test to be applied.
Thus, there has to be a finding of fact, as to, whether, the owner or the insured had taken reasonable care.

Hence, the Tribunal will have to decide the dispute,
as to, whether, the insurer has proved its defence.

While adjudicating the said claim if the Tribunal concludes that the insurer has satisfactorily proved its defence in accordance with Section 149(2)
(a) of the Act, the Tribunal can direct that the insurer is liable to be reimbursed by the insured for the compensation and other amounts which it has been compelled to pay to the third party as per the award of the Tribunal having regard to the mandate of section 149(1) of the Act."

The Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Swaran Singh and Others reported in (2004) 3 SCC 297 cited supra has categorically held that to avoid its liability towards insured, the insurer has to prove that the insured was guilty of negligence and failed to exercise reasonable care in the matter of fulfilling the condition of the policy regarding use of vehicles by duly licensed driver or one who was not disqualified to drive at the relevant time.

Further at para 110 the Hon'ble Apex Court has observed thus:
(iii) The breach of policy condition e.g., disqualification of driver or invalid driving licence of the driver, as contained in sub-section (2)(a)(ii) of section 149, have to be proved to have been committed by the insured for avoiding liability by the insurer.

Mere absence, fake or invalid driving licence or disqualification of the driver for driving at the relevant time, are not in themselves defences available to the insurer Ramachandra vs Icici Lomb Gen Ins Co Ltd on 10 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/139945407/
9 against either the insured or the third parties.

To avoid its liability towards insured,
the insurer has to prove that the insured was guilty of negligence and failed to exercise reasonable care in the matter of fulfilling the condition of the policy regarding use of vehicles by duly licensed driver or one who was not disqualified to drive at the relevant time.

31. No doubt the respondent No.1 insurance company has proved that the rider of vehicle bearing No. KA-05-KF-9680 did not possess license, but the above decision makes it clear that the respondent No.1 was required to prove that the insured was negligent or did not exercise reasonable care which is not proved.

Thereby fortifying the view taken by this court that the respondent No.1 should make good the compensation amount to the petitioner and then proceed against the respondent No.2 i.e., the owner to recover the same.

39. For the foregoing reasons this court finds no hesitation in holding that the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner and the respondent No.1 being the insurer shall pay the compensation amount to the petitioner with liberty to recover the same from respondent No.2 owner.

Accordingly, Issue No.2 is held in the partly affirmative and it is held that the petitioner is entitled for compensation along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum and this issue is answered accordingly.
32. ISSUE NO.3:

For the foregoing reasons, I proceed to pass the following;
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner U/s. 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.80,000/-
(Rupees Eighty thousand only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition till the realization from respondents.
The respondent No.1 - insurance company is directed to deposit the compensation amount within 60 days from the date of this order and recover the same from the respondent No.2 - owner.
Considering the quantum of amount awarded to petitioner, it is ordered to release the entire amount in his favour.
Advocate fee is fixed at 1,500/-.
Draw up award accordingly.

opennyai_summary.facts: The petitioner has filed this petition U/Sec.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident that occurred on 29-08-2018.
opennyai_summary.issue:
4. On the basis of the rival contention, the following issues are framed by this court:
1.
Whether the petitioner proves that, the petitioner sustained grievous injuries due to the actionable negligent riding of motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-05- KF-9680 by its rider, in RTA took place on 29.08.2018 at about 3.45 p.m. near Canara Bank (C.B.)

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Proceedings under Motor Vehicles Act are not akin to proceedings in a Civil Court.
Ramachandra vs Icici Lomb Gen Ins Co Ltd on 10 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/139945407/
4 14.
In a claim for compensation under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the claimant is to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and the standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by Hon'ble Supreme Court in the decision reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319 Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others.
Further the Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others (2009) 13 SCC 530, wherein it is held that, it was necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.
17. As per well settled principle of law, the standard of proof in the claim petition like the present is preponderance of the probability.
There are no grounds to disbelieve the case of petitioner in the absence of rebuttal evidence.
All the materials available on record leading to show that, petitioner has sustained injuries in the accident took place on 29-08-2018 which is caused by the driver of the Motorcycle bearing No.KA-05-KF- 9680 which belonging to respondent No.1.
There is no reason to discard the evidence of petitioner.
The petitioner has not made out any evidence or grounds to hold that he sustained the loss of income during the laid down period hence, in the absence of any evidence,
petitioner is not entitled for any amount under the head of loss of income during laid up period.
To establish the said fact, the respondent No.1 initially relied on Ex.P7 charge sheet wherein Sec.279, 338 of IPC and Sec.119 r/w 177 & 3(1) r/w 181 & 5 r/w 180 of IMV Act are invoked against the rider of vehicle bearing No. KA.05- KF-9680.
On perusal of the Ex.P7 the rider of the said offending vehicle bearing No. KA.05-KF-9680 was not having valid licence at the time of accident to drive the said vehicle.
Ramachandra vs Icici Lomb Gen Ins Co Ltd on 10 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/139945407/
7 26.
The respondent No.2 owner even though appeared not lead any evidence by denying the contents of charge sheet in this regard.
Thereby the respondent No.1 insurance company discharged its burden to hold that the rider of the vehicle bearing No. KA.05-KF-9680 was not having valid licence at the time of accident.
27. There is no dispute that at the time of accident the vehicle was covered with insurance.
But the violation of the condition of insurance policy is stands established.
As per Ex.R1 it contains the condition that it covers the risk provided the person driving the vehicle holds an effective and valid driving licence at the time of accident and is not disqualified from holding such licence.
In this case,
the respondent No.2 owner of the offending vehicle bearing No. KA.05-KF-9680 not contested the petition by adducing any evidence by showing that the rider was having driving license at the time of accident.
In other words, in order to avoid the liability towards the insured, the insurer has to prove that the insured was guilty of negligence and failed to exercise reasonable care in the matter of fulfilling the condition of policy regarding use of the vehicle by a duly licensed driver or one who was not disqualified to drive at the relevant time.
Thus,
burden of proof of establishing breach on the part of the owner of the vehicle is on the Insurance Company.
Even after proving breach of a policy condition regarding a valid licence by the driver or his qualification to drive during the relevant period on the part of the insured, the insurer would not be allowed to avoid his liability towards the insured unless the said breach or breaches is/are so "fundamental" as found to have contributed to the cause of the accident.
This is having regard to the "rule of main purpose" or "main purpose rule" i.e., even if there is a proof of the driver of a motor vehicle not being duly licenced at the time of the accident,
the said fact must be a cause for the accident.
In other words, the breach was so fundamental as to have contributed to the cause of the accident.
The doctrine of fundamental breach has been incorporated in Section 149 of the Act by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in order to give effect to the main purpose rule.
Thus, the exclusion clause or the defence of an insurer so as to avoid liability has been read down to the extent to which it is inconsistent to the main purpose of the contract.
Thus, there has to be a finding of fact, as to, whether, the owner or the insured had taken reasonable care.

Accordingly, Issue No.2 is held in the partly affirmative and it is held that the petitioner is entitled for compensation along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum and this issue is answered accordingly.
32. ISSUE NO.3:
For the foregoing reasons, I proceed to pass the following;
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner U/s. 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.
The petitioner is entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.80,000/-
(Rupees Eighty thousand only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition till the realization from respondents.
The respondent No.1 - insurance company is directed to deposit the compensation amount within 60 days from the date of this order and recover the same from the respondent No.2 - owner.
Considering the quantum of amount awarded to petitioner, it is ordered to release the entire amount in his favour.
Advocate fee is fixed at 1,500/-.
Draw up award accordingly.
